quests.sentence: Our neighbor drives a small red truck.
quests.hint: Subject first, then the verb, then the object with its describing words.
quests.explanation: Our neighbor (subject) drives (verb) a small red truck (object), following standard Subject-Verb-Object order.

quests.sentence: The baker bakes fresh bread daily.
quests.hint: Place the frequency word 'daily' at the very end.
quests.explanation: The baker (subject) bakes (verb) fresh bread (object), with daily added at the end to show frequency.

quests.sentence: The nurse helps sick patients every day.
quests.hint: Keep the subject and verb together, then add the object, then the frequency phrase.
quests.explanation: The nurse (subject) helps (verb) sick patients (object), followed by every day to show how often.

quests.sentence: There are two books on the shelf.
quests.hint: Start with 'There are' before the plural noun, then add the location.
quests.explanation: There are introduces the existence of something, followed by the plural noun books and its location.

quests.sentence: There is a spider on the wall.
quests.hint: Use 'There is' before a singular noun, then the location.
quests.explanation: There is introduces one thing, a spider, followed by its location on the wall.

quests.sentence: There are many students in the library.
quests.hint: 'There are' goes first with plural nouns, followed by quantity and location.
quests.explanation: There are begins the sentence, followed by many students and the location in the library.

quests.sentence: Her brother lost his new wallet.
quests.hint: Possessive words like 'her' and 'his' come right before the noun they describe.
quests.explanation: Her describes brother, and his describes wallet, each placed directly before its noun.

quests.sentence: Their parents sold their old house.
quests.hint: The possessive word 'their' goes before each noun it belongs to.
quests.explanation: Their appears before parents and again before old house, showing ownership in both places.

quests.sentence: My cousin painted her bedroom yellow.
quests.hint: Possessives go directly before the noun, and color words often come at the end.
quests.explanation: My describes cousin, her describes bedroom, and yellow describes the new color at the end.

quests.sentence: The manager explained the plan clearly.
quests.hint: The manner adverb 'clearly' goes at the end, after the object.
quests.explanation: Clearly describes how the manager explained, so it follows the object the plan.

quests.sentence: The workers finished the project quickly.
quests.hint: Place the manner adverb after the object, at the end of the sentence.
quests.explanation: Quickly tells us how the workers finished, positioned after the object the project.

quests.sentence: She organized the files carefully yesterday.
quests.hint: The manner adverb comes right after the object, before the time word.
quests.explanation: Carefully shows how she organized the files, and yesterday tells us when, in that order.

quests.sentence: The plane landed at the airport.
quests.hint: The place phrase comes right after the verb.
quests.explanation: At the airport tells us where the plane landed, placed after the verb.

quests.sentence: Our train arrived at the station.
quests.hint: Put the location phrase directly after the verb arrived.
quests.explanation: At the station shows the place, coming right after the verb arrived.

quests.sentence: We stayed in a cozy cabin.
quests.hint: The place phrase follows the verb, with the adjective before the noun.
quests.explanation: In a cozy cabin tells us where we stayed, with cozy describing cabin.

quests.sentence: He washed the dishes and cleaned the counter.
quests.hint: The word 'and' connects two actions done by the same subject.
quests.explanation: And joins two verb phrases, washed the dishes and cleaned the counter, done by the same subject he.

quests.sentence: She wanted pizza but ordered a salad.
quests.hint: 'But' shows a contrast between two actions by the same subject.
quests.explanation: But connects two contrasting ideas: what she wanted and what she actually ordered.

quests.sentence: They practiced hard and won the match.
quests.hint: 'And' links two actions in the order they happened.
quests.explanation: And joins practiced hard and won the match, two actions performed by the same subject.

quests.sentence: We visited an old castle last summer.
quests.hint: Subject, past verb, object, then the time expression at the end.
quests.explanation: We (subject) visited (past verb) an old castle (object), with last summer showing when.

quests.sentence: The band played their new song loudly.
quests.hint: Keep subject and verb together, then the object, then the manner adverb.
quests.explanation: The band (subject) played (verb) their new song (object), with loudly describing how.

quests.sentence: I watched an exciting soccer game yesterday.
quests.hint: Place the adjective before the noun, and the time word at the end.
quests.explanation: Exciting describes soccer game, and yesterday tells us when I watched it.

quests.sentence: She bought a shiny new laptop.
quests.hint: Describing words about appearance usually come before words about age, like 'new'.
quests.explanation: Shiny (appearance) comes before new (age), and both are placed before the noun laptop.

quests.sentence: He owns a sleek black smartphone.
quests.hint: Shape or style words come before color words, then the noun.
quests.explanation: Sleek describes style, black is the color, and both come before the noun smartphone.

quests.sentence: I found a tiny silver coin.
quests.hint: Size words like 'tiny' come before color or material words like 'silver'.
quests.explanation: Tiny (size) comes before silver (color), and both come before the noun coin.

quests.sentence: She takes medicine after every meal.
quests.hint: The time phrase 'after every meal' comes at the end.
quests.explanation: After every meal tells us when she takes medicine, following the object medicine.

quests.sentence: He exercises at the gym daily.
quests.hint: Place the location phrase before the frequency word at the end.
quests.explanation: At the gym shows the place, and daily shows how often, in that order.

quests.sentence: We rested in the park after lunch.
quests.hint: The place phrase comes before the time phrase at the end.
quests.explanation: In the park tells us where, and after lunch tells us when, both following the verb rested.

quests.sentence: The excited children ran quickly toward the playground.
quests.hint: Combine the adjective and subject, then the verb, the manner adverb, and the place.
quests.explanation: This review sentence links an adjective, subject, verb, manner adverb, and place phrase in standard order.

quests.sentence: Our whole family enjoyed the delicious dinner together.
quests.hint: Keep the subject and its describing words together before the verb.
quests.explanation: This sentence reviews Subject-Verb-Object order along with an adjective (delicious) and a closing adverb (together).

quests.sentence: The young athlete trained hard every single day.
quests.hint: Subject with adjective, then verb, then manner word, then the frequency phrase.
quests.explanation: This checkpoint sentence combines an adjective, past-tense verb, manner adverb, and frequency phrase in natural order.
